text.p: A Florida man who confessed to strangling and beating a woman to death in a Houston motel in 1982 was executed Tuesday at the Huntsville State Prison.

Robert West, 35, was sentenced to die for the murder of Deanna Klaus, a 22-year-old waitress who lived one floor below West at the Memorial Park Motel. She was strangled with a belt and then beaten and stabbed with a wooden club.

"I would like to apologise for all the pain and suffering I have put you all through. I hope this will give you closure now and later on down the line," West said as he lay strapped to a gurney in the death chamber. He was injected with a dose of lethal chemicals and died shortly after 6:30 p.m. CDT.

West became the 25th condemned inmate put to death this year in Texas, extending the state's record for executions in a single year. Texas leads the nation with 132 executions since the death penalty was reinstated by the U.S. Supreme Court in 1976.

The Supreme Court rejected an 11th hour appeal by West, who confessed to murdering Klaus during a drug-induced rage over the recent murder of a friend in Montrose, a gay Houston neighbourhood where he and the victim lived.

Several witnesses saw West emerge from Klaus' room soaked in blood, and he was arrested less than an hour after police found her body. She had been stripped naked, bound at her wrists and ankles and strangled, beaten and stabbed.

West spent his final day on death row visiting with a girlfriend, Jessica Kelly from England. He ordered a last meal of a cheeseburger, french fries and a Coca-Cola. His request for a pack of cigarettes was denied because of the prison's no-smoking policy, a prison spokesman said.

Texas in June eclipsed its previous record of 19 executions in a year, and could put as many as 40 inmates to death this year after a state court upheld a new law limiting death row appeals, officials said.
The spate of executions, including last month's of a Mexican citizen sentenced to die for the 1985 murder of a Texas man, has drawn protests from international human rights groups.
